Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really helpful. I shared a rough architecture diagram and a draft mutual-action plan (attached) so our infra and security teams have something to review. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the POC and timeline: 

- SDK & auth: Our app runs the inference calls from a server-side service (NodeJS). We prefer short-lived credentials (OIDC/service account) and want minimal client-side secrets. Can you confirm supported auth modes (API key, service account + JWT, mTLS) and any example server-side refresh logic?

- Routing & policy: We liked the idea of routing by latency/cost tiers. Our SLA target for interactive search is p95 < 200ms; for batch reranking it's OK to be slower. We also want a fallback chain so heavy requests fall back to smaller quantized variants. Can you share recommended policy patterns (latency threshold vs cost cap) and a starting fallback chain?

- Structured output / tool calling: We'll rely on tool calling for lookups and want JSON-enforced outputs for downstream processing. Any guidance on combining function calls with rerankers/embeddings?

- Embeddings & reranker: We'll seed a 100k doc index and want to keep embedding compute under a cost threshold. Are there suggested batch sizes, embedding models, and recommendation for when to run a reranker vs pure semantic similarity?

- Infra reqs: We'll need to provision a staging VPC and a service account with restricted roles if possible. Do you have a list of required ports/egress or a Terraform module?

Next steps: can we schedule a 60-min technical workshop with your integration engineer and our platform team? Prefer Thu (Dec 3) morning PST.

Attachments: redwood-architecture-diagram.pdf, acme-mop-draft.xlsx

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Search Engineering | ACME Corp

Thanks Samira — really appreciate the detailed notes and the attachments. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so your team can prep: 

Recap & recommended starting configuration:
1) SDK & auth
   - Supported auth modes: API key (quickstart), service-account via JWT/OIDC (recommended for server-side), and mTLS for Private deployments.
   - We'll share a short NodeJS example for server-side token refresh (service account -> short-lived token). For Private/VPC customers we recommend mTLS + customer-managed KMS for keys.

2) Model routing & policy (starter pattern)
   - Region routing: prefer us-west primary, failover to us-east if capacity constrained.
   - Latency policy: p95 target 250ms as a safe default for interactive workloads; can tighten to 200ms after load testing.
   - Cost policy: per-route token cap + route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical calls.
   - Fallback chain (example): rdx-gptq-small -> rdx-gptq-medium -> rdx-3b-quant -> rdx-8b (full)

3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - Use function/tool calling with explicit JSON schema validation. If an output fails validation, route to a higher-quality model or trigger a deterministic fallback.

4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Embedding model: embeddings-v2 (balanced cost/quality). Start with batch size 128–256 for CPU/GPU tradeoffs; tune per-job.
   - Reranker pattern: use semantic similarity (ANN) for top-200 recall, then rerank top-20 with a cross-encoder reranker for precision.

5) Infra & access
   - We'll provide a staging Terraform snippet and a required IAM role template. For network: outbound HTTPS (443) and optional VPN/peering for Private.

Proposed next step: 60-min technical workshop to run through SDK setup, auth, and draft routing policies. Dev Patel and Marcus Lin (our integration leads) will join. We have availability Thu Dec 3 9:00–11:30 PST; please confirm a 60-min slot.

I attached a short sample routing config and a link to the mutual-action plan in HubSpot for milestone tracking.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Samira — quick technical notes ahead of the workshop. Copying key config snippets and requirements so your platform team can review: 

1) NodeJS SDK/auth example (server-side, service account flow)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ endpoint: process.env.RW_ENDPOINT, token: await fetchShortLivedToken() });

2) Sample routing policy (YAML) — starter: 
route: interactive-search
  priority: latency
  p95_target_ms: 250
  fallback_chain:
    - rdx-gptq-small
    - rdx-gptq-medium
    - rdx-8b
  cost_cap_per_request_usd: 0.02

3) Deployment notes:
- Use prefix/KV caching for query-heavy interactive workloads to reduce token costs.
- Autoscaler: set CPU/GPU concurrency to maintain p95 target under expected qps; we'll suggest initial concurrency based on your qps numbers in the workshop.
- Embeddings: recommend batched upserts (size 128) with incremental indexing.

4) Security/access:
- For staging we need a service account email and an allowed CIDR for testing if you want to restrict.
- Provide a short-lived token endpoint (OIDC) or we can accept a service-account JSON for initial POC with limited TTL.

Let us know if you want us to pre-populate a sample reranker pipeline (ANN index -> cross-encoder) using a 10k sample dataset before the call. We can also attach the Terraform snippet and the sample-routing-config.yaml to the HubSpot record.

Thanks,
